raw_response:
I will mostly do what has worked for me around Quzhou, and I will only adjust a little for cost and labor. I farm 15 mu by myself, so I cannot make the plan too fancy. Last year and the years before, if I underfed a crop, I could see the loss right away, and that hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. I have well water, so I will use that to keep the important stages from drying out. For wheat, I will keep the land flatter and feed it steadily because that crop needs a safe yield. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and push nitrogen a bit because neighbors here do that and maize responds when water is available. For stevia, I will put more effort into fertilizer, irrigation, and sprays because it is the cash crop and if the leaves stay clean and growing, the money is better. I will still watch costs, so I will not over-scatter inputs, but I will not go light where yield can be lost.
